topic: Explain the GPU calculator formula, its full-utilization assumption and why a rental reference differs from contributor rewards.

localizations.title: What the GPU calculator actually tells you
localizations.excerpt: GPU hours, an hourly rate and a 30-day month. Understand the simple calculation, its assumptions and the difference between rental value and contributor rewards.
localizations.seoTitle: Understand GPU compute estimates and rewards | Mycellios
localizations.seoDescription: See how the Mycellios GPU calculator uses daily hours and an hourly rate, what costs it excludes and why a rental estimate is not a promised contributor payout.
localizations.imageAlt: Computers and server hardware joined by an illustrated fungal network.
localizations.contentHtml:
Spare GPU time can be described in hours. Assign an hourly rate to those hours and you have a value to explore. That is the starting point of the Mycellios GPU calculator.

The result is a monthly rental reference. It helps explain the scale of a compute scenario; it does not tell you that your device will receive work for every available hour or that Mycellios will pay the displayed amount.

The calculation in one line

Daily GPU hours × 30 days × hourly rate = monthly gross reference.

For an arithmetic example, choose 8 hours a day and enter a hypothetical rate of $0.10 per GPU-hour:

8 hours/day × 30 days = 240 GPU-hours
240 GPU-hours × $0.10/hour = $24.00

The $0.10 rate is an example chosen to explain the formula, not an approved Mycellios payout rate. The $24 result assumes that every one of the 240 selected hours is rented at that rate.

What the GPU selection changes

Selecting a GPU selects an indicative hourly rental reference for that model. The calculator then multiplies that rate by your chosen hours.

This is not a benchmark of your particular computer. It does not measure performance, test available memory, check drivers or establish that a model will run on your device. It also does not confirm that your GPU is supported by the contribution runtime you install.

Check the calculation details to review the rate used. You can enter your own hourly rate to explore a different scenario; changing it changes the arithmetic, not the terms of any service or reward program.

Available time is different from completed work

A computer can be online and available without being assigned a task. Demand, model compatibility, capacity requirements and the runtime all affect whether work can be placed on a device.

The calculator deliberately uses a simple assumption: all selected hours are rented. It does not predict demand or apply a hidden utilization forecast. If fewer hours are used, the fully rented reference no longer describes that actual usage.

The result comes before costs

The displayed figure excludes electricity, fees and taxes. Those costs are not inferred from a GPU name, and the calculator does not measure your computer's power use.

For your own analysis, keep the rental reference and operating costs separate. A gross reference and a net result answer different questions. Increasing available hours increases the reference mathematically; it does not guarantee a better real-world outcome.

Rental references, Credits and Spore

A rental reference describes a scenario for the cost of compute. An actual contributor reward requires a defined policy and evidence of the work that qualifies under it.

Mycellios contributor payouts are marked coming soon. The calculator does not promise a withdrawal amount, a payment schedule or a conversion into Spore.

Credits and Spore also have different roles. Credits are the internal account unit used for usage and balances. Spore is the separate token concept. No public token or on-chain contributor settlement is active under the current documented readiness state.

Use the number as a question to investigate

Start by choosing the GPU you actually have and a realistic window when the computer could be available. Open the calculation details, review the rate and compare a few schedules.

Then check the Rewards page for the current program status and compute contribution options for supported setup routes. You can also try the calculator with the assumptions visible.

sourceNotes.note: Reviewed the local calculator implementation: daily hours times 30 days times selected or custom hourly rate, with a full-rental assumption and no performance inference. The article uses its own explicit hypothetical rate instead of repeating a changing provider quote.
Reviewed economic/token status and capability boundaries. Contributor payouts remain coming soon; Credits and Spore are distinct and no public-token or withdrawal promise is made.
